title: Four Winters and One Short Letter
subtitle: 战争与和平 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 战争与和平（人与社会·历史、社会与文化）
meta: 主题语境：战争与和平（人与社会·历史、社会与文化）　|　核心词汇：enemy　|　正文 342 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 enemy 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1914 my great-uncle ① made an enemy that no officer in the regiment would have named, and he said the making was the whole of the winter. The ② enemy, meaning the man himself and not the army, ran four winters and stayed unnamed in the book; an enemy, he said, is the only thing in a regiment that is judged by how long it is left unnamed.

Every ③ enemy in that regiment had the same short letter beside it, and the ④ enemy at the far side, meaning the one they kept for the border and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. An enemy, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to name; my great-uncle said the naming is the part that fills four winters.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the enemy was the whole of the war, meaning the army and not the man. The ⑥ enemy, meaning the army and not any of that, is the only thing in a war that everybody waits for and nobody names; enemy, he said, is either something you make or the only word that means both a man and an army. He said the army is the part they remember.

By 1918 the ⑦ enemy had become a line in a treaty, and the treaty had become an argument about the short letter. The ⑧ enemy of the whole thing, my great-uncle wrote in January, was one regiment and four winters of naming; enemy, he said, is either the one at the far side or the reason you learned to name. He said the naming was never mentioned.

The ⑨ enemy I remember is the one named in the treaty, which closed in 1920 and is still described as the quietest in the regiment. An ⑩ enemy, my mother said in 1922, is the only one that improves by being named; every enemy, she said, is an army that has agreed to look like a man. She said the army was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 敌人（指团里每一个人旁边的那一个）
B. n. 敌人（指那个人本身，与敌军相对）
C. 固定搭配：make an enemy 树敌；结怨
D. n. 敌人（指留给边境的那一个）
E. n. 敌人（抽象总称，指一支队伍的敌对之事）
F. n. 敌人（指条约上写到、被标名的那一个）
G. n. 敌军；敌国（指战争里人人都等却无人命名的那样东西）
H. n. 敌军（抽象总称，指人人都等却无人命名的那种力量）

items.q: made an enemy that no officer in the regiment would have named
The enemy, meaning the man himself and not the army
the enemy at the far side
the enemy was the whole of the war
the enemy had become a line in a treaty
The enemy of the whole thing
An enemy, my mother said in 1922

answers.why: make an enemy 意为“树敌、结怨”，1914 年曾叔父树了一个团里没有一位军官肯说出口的敌人。
enemy 意为“敌人”，指那个人本身而不是那支军队，它经过了四个冬天而在簿子上没有名字。
enemy 意为“敌人”，指那个团里每一个人身边的那一个，每一个旁边都有同一封短短的信。
enemy 意为“敌人”，指他们留给边境的那一个，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
enemy 意为“敌军、敌国”，指战争里人人都等却无人命名的那样东西，叔叔说这个敌军就是那场战争的全部。
enemy 意为“敌军”，指人人都等却无人命名的那种力量而不是那个人，是战争里人人都等、却无人命名的东西。
enemy 意为“敌人”，指条约上写到、被标名的那一个，到 1918 年这一个成了条约里的一行。
enemy 意为“敌人”，曾叔父一月写道，整件事的敌对之事是一个团和四个冬天的命名。
enemy 意为“敌人”，我记得的是条约上标名的那一个，1920 年结束了，至今仍被说成团里最安静的一个。
enemy 为抽象总称，母亲 1922 年说，一个敌人是唯一会因为被好好命名而变得更好的东西。
